assertions.text: The pay table includes intermediate expected columns (e.g. Regular pay?, Overtime pay?, Premium pay?) so the reader can trace which rule contributes what — not just a single total Weekly pay? column.
assertions.evidence: Table columns are: Weekday hrs, Sunday hrs, Holiday hrs, Rate, Total pay? — no intermediate columns for Regular pay, Overtime pay, or Premium pay

assertions.text: The error/rejection table has an expected column (e.g. 'Throws?' or 'Exception?') specifying the exception type per row — rather than hardcoding the exception type in @Description or the method name.
assertions.evidence: Error table includes 'Throws?' column with 'IllegalArgumentException' value per row

assertions.text: Overtime threshold boundary is covered: at least a value at the threshold (40) and just above (41 or similar). Not just values well below and well above.
assertions.evidence: Table includes 'Weekday hours at threshold | 40' and 'One overtime hour | 41'

assertions.text: A combined scenario is present: a row with weekday + Sunday + holiday hours, testing the composition of all hour types.
assertions.evidence: Row 'All pay types in one week | 42 | 4 | 4 | 20.00 | 1180.00' covers all three types

assertions.text: Error/edge cases covered: at least negative hours (floored at zero) and negative or missing rate (rejected).
assertions.evidence: Error table tests negative rate rejection, but no test row for negative weekday/Sunday/holiday hours floored to zero

assertions.text: Sunday and Holiday hour columns use empty cells (not 0) when those inputs are not relevant to a scenario — making it easier to spot which rows involve weekend/holiday hours. This is a readability preference; parameter types should be Integer (not int) to support null from blank cells.
assertions.evidence: Table uses '0' for unused columns (e.g., row 'Weekday hours under threshold | 35 | 0 | 0'); method signature uses 'int weekday...' not 'Integer'

assertions.text: Scenario names describe work patterns (e.g. 'Part-time', 'Five hours overtime', 'Full Sunday shift') — not 'Test case 1' or expected outcomes.
assertions.evidence: Scenarios like 'Significant overtime', 'Sunday with weekday overtime', 'All pay types in one week' describe work patterns, not test cases

assertions.text: Expected values in intermediate and total columns are arithmetically correct for every row, consistent with the formulas in @Description.
Value sets are only used where all values in the set produce the same expected result (e.g. any rate × 0 = 0). Not used where results would differ.
assertions.evidence: Error table uses '{0, 40}' for weekday hours with -1.00 rate; both should reject (same result)

assertions.text: @DisplayName is present on test methods, OR method names read as clear descriptive titles when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: Both methods have @DisplayName: 'Weekly pay calculation' and 'Reject negative hourly rate'

assertions.text: @Description is present on at least the pay calculation method and provides context beyond what the table rows already express — such as the overtime threshold (40 hours), premium multipliers (Sunday 2×, Holiday 2.5×), or other fixed assumptions not visible in the table. Does NOT merely restate the column names or summarise what the rows show.
assertions.evidence: @Description states 'weekday hours up to 40', 'beyond 40 × 1.5', 'Sunday hours × 2', 'holiday hours × 2', 'floor is zero' — all non-obvious rules

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: calculatesWeeklyPay has @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest in correct order; rejectsNegativeRate has @DisplayName, @TableTest

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses triple-quoted string """ with multi-line content, no concatenation

assertions.text: A row where the hourly rate is zero, showing that pay is zero regardless of hours worked. This is a distinct edge case from negative rate (which is rejected).
assertions.evidence: Row 'Zero hourly rate | 40 | 0 | 0 | 0.00 | 0.00' tests zero rate separately from negative rate

assertions.text: The test method body contains no if/ternary null-handling or parsing logic. Null-to-default conversion (e.g. blank Sunday hours → 0) is handled via a @TypeConverter method or a private helper, keeping the test method limited to arrange/act/assert.
assertions.evidence: Both test methods contain only direct assertions; no if/ternary logic or null-handling in the method bodies

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Weekday hours', 'Sunday hours', 'Hourly rate', 'Weekly pay?') — not implementation terms like 'weekdayHrs', 'int', 'param1'.
assertions.evidence: Column headers: 'Weekday hrs', 'Sunday hrs', 'Holiday hrs', 'Rate', 'Total pay?', 'Throws?' — all business-language terms

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules. Acceptable to use a single table only when the domain genuinely has a single concern.
assertions.evidence: Two separate methods: calculatesWeeklyPay (happy path) and rejectsNegativeRate (error handling)

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns. Fewer rows per table is expected when concerns are properly separated.
assertions.evidence: calculatesWeeklyPay has 12 focused rows covering boundaries/combinations; rejectsNegativeRate has 1 row (with value set) testing negative rate

assertions.text: Payable hours categorisation (1x regular, 1.5x overtime, 2x Sunday/holiday) and pay calculation (hours × rate) are in separate @TableTest methods
assertions.evidence: Single @TableTest method calculatesWeeklyPay combines both hour categorisation and final pay calculation; no separate method for categorisation logic
